title: Oriented Water Donor Temperature Contract

invariants.evidence: Adds one generic donor-temperature selector for the single SWAP5 architecture; no standalone/MultiSWAP/MODFLOW-specific kernel variant is created.
Production code has no files, paths, parsing, formats or unit-number dependencies.
The selector consumes an explicit transfer amount plus endpoint temperature availability/data and returns a separate result; it introduces no mixed persistent state/configuration object.
No persistent per-column dynamic or restart state is added.
No solver scratch, Newton vector, Jacobian or constitutive cache is introduced.
The scalar selector is layout-independent and trivially batchable, but SoA/SIMD/cache behavior is not benchmarked.
The selector is stateless and trial-safe, but commit/rollback-aware energy publication is a later composition concern.
Selection is deterministic and cheaply recomputable from the same signed amount and endpoint inputs with no hidden history.
No calendar or fixed timestep exists; the amount can belong to any qualified interval.
No coupling-window duration or midnight/day boundary is encoded.
The contract is explicitly designed for later conservation/coupling composition, but no coupling runtime is wired here.
No SWAP-MODFLOW head/flux contract is modified. Groundwater temperature, if needed later, must arrive through an explicit external interface rather than being inferred.
The signed water amount is preserved and never thresholded or altered; EB-I06 cannot create, destroy or rebalance water.
No groundwater response tangent or sensitivity is changed or added.
Donor selection is constant-cost local algebra and requires no additional SWAP solve or coupling iteration.
No heavy per-column object or persistent state is introduced, but large-batch MultiSWAP throughput is not measured.
A/B endpoints are generic and know nothing about MODFLOW-cell tile fractions or aggregation.
No deep-vadose component behavior is changed.
No transition between deep-vadose and direct coupling is changed.
The donor rule depends only on an oriented transfer amount and endpoint temperatures, not on a particular Richards implementation.
The contract supports future reuse of SWAP transport physics without importing legacy globals or module internals.
No HeadCalc or soil-water-solver internal arrays are referenced.
The donor/upwind rule is explicit physical/numerical transport semantics; no performance policy changes physics and no boundary temperature is silently invented.
The primitive itself is bounded constant-cost algebra, but bounded-cost behavior in complete difficult-column energy composition is not qualified here.
No reference solver or existing physics is replaced; current canonical remains intact.
The result exposes status, donor endpoint and availability explicitly, but runtime-wide diagnostics/provenance publication is deferred.
Unused columns incur no additional persistent state or workspace cost.
Mapping real processes to A/B, supplying external donor temperatures and aggregating tiles remain runtime/coupler/component responsibilities.
No .swp, filesystem, midnight, one-day, direct-MODFLOW or implicit boundary-temperature assumption is present.
EB-I06 is explicitly assessed against all 30 SWAP core architecture invariants in this audit.

hard_nonclaims: No full SWAP5 energy balance is qualified.
No Joule or heat-flux calculation is performed.
No external water-temperature source or inference rule is qualified.
No temporal averaging or flux-weighted donor-temperature quadrature is qualified.
No higher-order advection, mixing, dispersion or thermal equilibration during transit is represented.
No vapor or latent transport and no phase-change transport is represented.
Runtime commit/rollback publication, MultiSWAP throughput and bounded-cost behavior are not qualified.
Independent verification and canonical admission are not claimed.
